World Bank financing secured for health digitalization (63 units)
Span of Mozambique's first national Digital Health Strategy

overview: Mozambique's women's health innovation landscape is driven less by venture-backed startups than by government, donor, and NGO digital-health programs targeting one of the world's highest maternal mortality and cervical cancer burdens. Community health worker platforms such as upSCALE (Malaria Consortium, UNICEF, Ministry of Health) deliver antenatal, family planning, and child-health services by smartphone, while UNFPA, UNICEF, and PEPFAR anchor family planning, menstrual health, and HIV prevention. A new national Digital Health Strategy (2025-2034) and roughly USD 40M in World Bank financing signal a policy push toward telemedicine, AI, and hospital digitalization. The domestic femtech startup and gender-lens investment scene remains nascent compared with regional peers.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent developments center on national digital-health financing, family planning expansion, and menstrual health campaigns.

items.text: Mozambique secures about USD 40M from the World Bank to digitalize 63 health units, including a pilot first Digital Hospital at Mavalane General Hospital.
MISAU reaffirms digital transformation in health as a strategic priority, integrating AI and telemedicine to widen access.
For World Menstrual Hygiene Day, UNICEF with IOM, UNFPA, Helvetas and BeGirl ran school and community activities in Pemba to break menstruation taboos.
US directive pauses PEPFAR funding for oral PrEP except for pregnant and breastfeeding women, affecting HIV prevention for women in Mozambique.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Mozambique's first dedicated digital-health strategy sits alongside long-standing family planning and HIV prevention frameworks.

items.text: National Digital Health Strategy (ESD-MZ) 2025-2034 adopted, first planning cycle to 2029, targeting telemedicine, AI, and integrated health information systems.

Ministry of Health issues 2025 Guidelines for Combined Biomedical Prevention of HIV, STIs and Viral Hepatitis, adding long-acting PrEP options (injectable lenacapavir, cabotegravir, dapivirine vaginal ring).
Cervical Cancer Elimination Strategy developed with UNFPA support, building on the national cervical and breast cancer program (VIA screening, HPV testing via GeneXpert).
National Family Planning Strategy sets goal of raising modern contraceptive prevalence from 34.3% (2020) to 43.4% by 2030 and cutting adolescent pregnancy.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Momentum comes chiefly from donor-backed community digital-health platforms and an emerging national startup incubator.

items.text: upSCALE community digital-health platform (built on Dimagi's CommCare) scaled nationally, equipping community health workers (APEs) with smartphone job aides for family planning, antenatal, and postnatal care plus integrated child case management.
INCM (national communications regulator) launched ThinkLab, a technology incubator in Maputo to nurture startup innovation and digital transformation.
Ministry of Health partnered with C-Saude to develop an integrated Health Information System, strengthening data infrastructure for maternal and community health.
UNICEF-BeGirl menstrual hygiene initiative reached over 3,000 girls with education and 1,300 with reusable-product MHM kits, promoting local production and school retention.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Financing is donor and multilateral, not venture capital; grants target family planning, digitalization, and community health delivery.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The active organizations are ministries, UN agencies, and implementing NGOs delivering women's and maternal health at scale.

items.name: Ministry of Health (MISAU)
items.note: Owns the Digital Health Strategy 2025-2034, family planning, HIV prevention, and cervical cancer programs

items.name: Malaria Consortium
items.note: Lead developer of the upSCALE community digital-health platform with MISAU and UNICEF

items.name: Dimagi
items.note: Provides CommCare, the platform underpinning upSCALE's CHW maternal and child health apps

items.name: UNFPA Mozambique
items.note: Leads family planning, menstrual health, and cervical cancer elimination support

items.name: UNICEF Mozambique
items.note: Co-developed upSCALE and runs the BeGirl menstrual hygiene management program

items.name: BeGirl
items.note: Menstrual product and education partner in UNICEF's MHM initiative, promoting reusable products

items.name: C-Saude
items.note: Partnering with MISAU on an integrated national Health Information System

items.name: ThinkLab (INCM)
items.note: National technology incubator launched 2025 in Maputo for startup innovation

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Capital for women's health comes overwhelmingly from bilateral donors and multilaterals rather than private funds.

items.name: World Bank
items.role: USD 40M for health-system digitalization including hospital pilots

items.name: Embassy of Ireland / Irish Aid
items.role: EUR 6M for UNFPA family planning and reproductive health project

items.name: PEPFAR (US Government)
items.role: Funds HIV prevention, PrEP scale-up, and PMTCT for women and pregnant mothers

items.name: UK Aid via UNICEF
items.role: Financed expansion and scale-up of the upSCALE community digital-health platform
